query: What are the real-world risks and benefits of using synthetic data to train or fine-tune large language models? Focus on data quality, bias, and evaluation.

sub_questions.text: What evidence shows that synthetic data improves data quality for training large language models?
How can synthetic data reduce bias in large language models according to real-world case studies?
What are the limitations of synthetic data in accurately representing real-world language patterns?
In what scenarios has synthetic data failed to generalize well in evaluations of large language models?
What evaluation metrics are most effective for assessing the impact of synthetic data on model performance?
